passages.text: At standard atmospheric pressure, which is the pressure found at sea level, pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius, or 212 degrees Fahrenheit. This temperature is known as the normal boiling point of water.
Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius, or 32 degrees Fahrenheit, at sea level. Adding salt lowers the freezing point, which is why salt is spread on icy roads in winter.

At high altitude the air pressure is lower, so water boils at a lower temperature. In Denver, about 1,600 metres above sea level, water boils at roughly 95 degrees Celsius, and food takes longer to cook.

Canberra is the capital city of Australia. It was purpose-built as the national capital in the early twentieth century, as a compromise between the rival cities of Sydney and Melbourne, and is home to Parliament House.

Sydney is the largest and most populous city in Australia and the capital of the state of New South Wales. It is famous for the Sydney Opera House and the Harbour Bridge, but it is not the national capital.
Melbourne is the capital of the Australian state of Victoria. It served as the temporary seat of the federal government from 1901 until 1927, when parliament moved to its permanent home.

Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy. Using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide, they produce glucose and release oxygen as a by-product.
Cellular respiration is the process cells use to release energy from glucose. In the presence of oxygen, glucose is broken down into carbon dioxide and water, and the energy is stored as ATP.
Chlorophyll is the green pigment found in the chloroplasts of plant cells. It absorbs mostly red and blue light and reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.
The adult human skeleton is made up of 206 bones. They provide structure, protect organs, anchor muscles and store calcium. The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest and strongest of them.
A newborn baby has around 270 to 300 bones. Many of these are made partly of cartilage and gradually fuse together as the child grows, which is why adults have fewer.
The human body contains more than 600 skeletal muscles, which make up roughly forty percent of body weight. Muscles work in pairs to move the bones they are attached to.

Pride and Prejudice is a novel by the English author Jane Austen, first published in 1813. It follows Elizabeth Bennet and her relationship with the wealthy Mr Darcy, and is one of the best-loved books in English literature.
Jane Eyre is a novel by Charlotte Bronte, published in 1847 under the pen name Currer Bell. It tells the story of an orphaned governess and her employer, Mr Rochester.
Emma, published in 1815, is a comic novel about a young woman who enjoys matchmaking among her neighbours. Its author also wrote Sense and Sensibility and Persuasion.

Ocean tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon on the Earth's water. The Sun also contributes, to a lesser extent. As the Earth rotates, most coasts experience two high tides and two low tides each day.
Most ocean waves are created by wind blowing across the surface of the water. The size of a wave depends on the wind speed, how long it blows and the distance of open water it travels over.

A tsunami is a series of very long waves caused by a sudden displacement of the ocean, usually by an undersea earthquake. Tsunamis are sometimes wrongly called tidal waves, but they have nothing to do with tides.

The speed of light in a vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second, or about 299,792 kilometres per second. It is usually written as c and is the upper limit for the speed of matter and information.
Sound travels through dry air at about 343 metres per second at 20 degrees Celsius. It moves faster through water and faster still through solids such as steel.
A light-year is a unit of distance, not time. It is the distance that light travels in one year, which is roughly 9.46 trillion kilometres.

The central processing unit, or CPU, is often called the brain of the computer. It fetches, decodes and executes program instructions, carrying out the arithmetic and logic operations that make software run.

Random access memory, or RAM, is a computer's short-term memory. It holds the data and programs that are currently in use so they can be reached quickly, and it is cleared when the power is turned off.
A graphics processing unit, or GPU, is a chip designed to render images and video. Because it can do many calculations in parallel, it is also widely used for training machine learning models.
The Earth takes about 365.25 days to complete one orbit around the Sun. The extra quarter of a day is why a leap day is added to the calendar every four years.
The Earth rotates once on its axis roughly every 24 hours, which gives us day and night. The axis is tilted by about 23.5 degrees, and this tilt causes the seasons.
The Moon takes about 27.3 days to orbit the Earth. Because the Earth is also moving around the Sun, the cycle of lunar phases from one full moon to the next takes about 29.5 days.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system. It is a gas giant with a mass more than twice that of all the other planets combined, and it is known for its Great Red Spot, a giant storm.
Saturn is the second-largest planet in the solar system and is best known for its bright system of rings, which are made mostly of ice particles with some rock and dust.
Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system and the closest to the Sun. It has almost no atmosphere, so its surface swings between extreme heat and extreme cold.

Common symptoms of dehydration include feeling thirsty, dark yellow urine, a dry mouth, tiredness, dizziness and headache. Severe dehydration can cause confusion and a rapid heartbeat and needs urgent medical attention.
How much water a person needs depends on their size, activity and the climate. A common guideline for adults is around two to three litres of fluid a day from drinks and food combined.

Heat stroke happens when the body can no longer control its temperature, which rises quickly to 40 degrees Celsius or more. The skin may feel hot and dry, and the person may become confused or collapse.

Bacteria are single-celled living organisms that can reproduce on their own, and many are harmless or helpful. Viruses are much smaller and are not cells; a virus can only reproduce by infecting a host cell and using its machinery.
Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them from growing. They do not work against colds, flu or other viral infections, and overusing them leads to antibiotic resistance.

Vaccines work by training the immune system. A vaccine contains a harmless part or a weakened form of a pathogen, which prompts the body to make antibodies and memory cells so it can respond quickly if it meets the real germ later.

World War II ended in 1945. Germany surrendered in May of that year, bringing the war in Europe to a close, and Japan formally surrendered on 2 September 1945 after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
World War I ended on 11 November 1918, when an armistice was signed between the Allies and Germany. The Treaty of Versailles, signed the following year, formally set the peace terms.
World War II began on 1 September 1939, when Germany invaded Poland. Britain and France declared war on Germany two days later.

In economics, inflation is a general increase in the prices of goods and services over time. As prices rise, each unit of currency buys less, so inflation reduces the purchasing power of money. It is commonly measured with a consumer price index.

Deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level. Although cheaper goods sound appealing, deflation can lead people to delay spending, which slows the economy and raises the real burden of debt.

Central banks set a benchmark interest rate to influence borrowing and spending. Raising the rate makes loans more expensive and tends to cool demand, while lowering it encourages borrowing and investment.
Mount Everest, in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and China, is the tallest mountain in the world above sea level. Its summit is about 8,849 metres, or 29,032 feet, high.
K2, on the border between Pakistan and China, is the second-highest mountain on Earth at 8,611 metres. It is considered a much harder climb than Everest.

Measured from its base on the ocean floor to its summit, Mauna Kea in Hawaii rises more than 10,000 metres. Most of that height is hidden under the sea, so only about 4,200 metres stands above the water.

Sunlight is scattered by the gas molecules in the atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths such as blue are scattered far more strongly than longer red wavelengths, an effect called Rayleigh scattering, and this scattered light is what gives the daytime sky its colour.

At sunset, sunlight passes through much more of the atmosphere before it reaches your eyes. Most of the blue light is scattered away along the path, leaving the reds and oranges that colour the evening sky.
The sea looks blue mainly because water absorbs red, orange and yellow light more strongly than blue. The blue light penetrates deeper and is scattered back toward the surface.
Guacamole is a Mexican dip whose main ingredient is ripe avocado, mashed with lime juice and salt. Chopped onion, coriander, tomato and chilli are often added.
Salsa is a Mexican sauce usually made from chopped tomatoes, onion, chilli peppers, coriander and lime juice. It is served with tortilla chips or used as a topping.
Hummus is a Middle Eastern dip made from cooked, mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon juice, garlic and olive oil.

To keep a notebook computer cool, clean the dust out of the air vents and fan, and use it on a hard, flat surface rather than a bed or cushion that blocks airflow. A cooling pad and closing demanding programs also bring temperatures down.
To make a laptop battery last longer, lower the screen brightness, switch on the battery saver mode and close background apps. Avoid leaving the battery fully drained for long periods.
If your phone is overheating, take it out of direct sunlight, remove the case and stop charging it until it cools. Do not put a hot phone in the fridge or freezer, because condensation can damage it.
A baby kangaroo is called a joey. It is born tiny and undeveloped and crawls into its mother's pouch, where it stays and feeds for several months before it starts to venture out.
Koalas are tree-dwelling marsupials found in eastern Australia. They feed almost entirely on eucalyptus leaves and sleep for up to twenty hours a day.
Kangaroos live across most of Australia, in grasslands, woodland and scrub. Adult male red kangaroos can stand close to two metres tall and travel in groups called mobs.
